{
  "findings": [

      "file": "app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss",
      "line": 239,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Dark-theme badge notification background may have very low contrast with its text",
      "body": ".badge-notification sets its text color to $secondary, while this change makes its background dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)). In a dark scheme, $secondary is the dark background/text color, so the dark-theme branch produces a dark background with dark text. The previous primary-based light background gave contrast with $secondary text; the new value can make notification counts hard or impossible to read."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss",
      "line": 291,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Embedded-post author link color appears inverted, reducing contrast",
      "body": "The rule for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a previously used scale-color($primary, 30%). It was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)), which makes the light-theme color much lighter and the dark-theme color much darker. Comparable author/name links use 30% in light schemes and 70% of $secondary in dark schemes, so this looks reversed and will make the link faint in both themes."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss",
      "line": 102,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Mobile custom-message-length uses inverted light/dark lightness values",
      "body": ".custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%)). The desktop modal uses 70% for light schemes and 30% for dark schemes for this subtle caption. The mobile change therefore changes the light-theme appearance and likely provides the wrong dark-theme contrast; it should probably remain primary 70% / secondary 30% if the intent is to preserve the existing visual hierarchy."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss",
      "line": 182,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Mobile topic-map heading color was changed in light theme as well as dark theme",
      "body": ".topic-map h3 originally used scale-color($primary, 20%). The change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%)), which lightens the heading substantially in light schemes and does not use the expected high-lightness secondary value for dark schemes. The desktop equivalent preserves the 20% light value and uses 80% for dark schemes, so this looks like an incorrect replacement rather than a dark-theme-only fix."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss",

      "body": "In .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification, the color remains scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while nearby topic-list text colors were converted to dark-light-choose with a $secondary-based dark-theme value. This leaves one similar text color using the old primary-based calculation, causing inconsistent dark-theme styling."

findings.title: Dark-theme badge notification background may have very low contrast with its text
findings.body: .badge-notification sets its text color to $secondary, while this change makes its background dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)). In a dark scheme, $secondary is the dark background/text color, so the dark-theme branch produces a dark background with dark text. The previous primary-based light background gave contrast with $secondary text; the new value can make notification counts hard or impossible to read.

findings.title: Embedded-post author link color appears inverted, reducing contrast
findings.body: The rule for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a previously used scale-color($primary, 30%). It was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)), which makes the light-theme color much lighter and the dark-theme color much darker. Comparable author/name links use 30% in light schemes and 70% of $secondary in dark schemes, so this looks reversed and will make the link faint in both themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length uses inverted light/dark lightness values
findings.body: .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%)). The desktop modal uses 70% for light schemes and 30% for dark schemes for this subtle caption. The mobile change therefore changes the light-theme appearance and likely provides the wrong dark-theme contrast; it should probably remain primary 70% / secondary 30% if the intent is to preserve the existing visual hierarchy.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading color was changed in light theme as well as dark theme
findings.body: .topic-map h3 originally used scale-color($primary, 20%). The change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%)), which lightens the heading substantially in light schemes and does not use the expected high-lightness secondary value for dark schemes. The desktop equivalent preserves the 20% light value and uses 80% for dark schemes, so this looks like an incorrect replacement rather than a dark-theme-only fix.

findings.title: Category badge notification color still uses only $primary
findings.body: In .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification, the color remains scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while nearby topic-list text colors were converted to dark-light-choose with a $secondary-based dark-theme value. This leaves one similar text color using the old primary-based calculation, causing inconsistent dark-theme styling.
